key_insight: For linear entanglement-assisted stabilizer codes, the standard quantum Singleton bound holds or can be violated depending on the recovery-set size relative to twice the number of logical qudits.
engineering_relevance: The results clarify when the standard bound reliably estimates shared-entanglement requirements and when code designs can consume fewer entangled pairs than it predicts.
method: Classify validity and violation by the number of qudits needed for recovery together with the receiver’s entangled-pair halves.
Bound violations using classical MDS code lengths and codes with specified Singleton defect.
Construct extremal codes from polynomial values and derivatives on the projective line.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical bounds, constructions attaining them in specified regimes, and Lean-formalized proofs apart from cited MDS lengths, rather than hardware experiments.
watch_item: Maximum-violation attainability depends on field size and applicable classical code-length results; practical implementation costs are not evaluated.
paper_title: Validity and maximum violation of the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound for linear stabilizer codes
